subject.title: fix(agents): make unrestricted host writes atomic

question: Should unrestricted host writes preserve successful writes to hard-linked and metadata-bearing files, or is rejecting/changing those existing host-file contracts an intentional compatibility policy?
rationale: Atomic inode replacement cannot retain every property of an existing inode, while the old direct write retained link identity and host metadata. The intended compatibility boundary is a product and security decision, not something the patch can infer safely.

options.title: Preserve existing contracts
options.body: Retain support for hard-linked and metadata-bearing files through a compatible fallback or complete metadata-preservation implementation, with regression proof.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed replacement
options.body: Accept hard-link rejection and metadata loss as the new unrestricted-write behavior, document the upgrade impact, and obtain explicit owner approval.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Land only a bounded staging change for targets whose metadata contract can be preserved, leaving the remaining cases on the existing path until a supported design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing contracts
recommendation.body: Retain support for hard-linked and metadata-bearing files through a compatible fallback or complete metadata-preservation implementation, with regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The patch author has already investigated the host-write behavior and can provide the relevant compatibility implementation or clarify the intended boundary.
